title: Derived support sections commute with etale-proetale direct image
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], on small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Derived categories are unbounded localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $C\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Write $H^	au_{T,C}=R\Gamma_C(T_	au,-)$ for the right derived kernel-of-restriction functor [def-pur-support-cohomology], on all complexes computed with K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For every $N\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$b_{C,N}:H^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}(R
u_{T,*}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}(N).$$
Its normalization is the identity, on a K-injective representative $J$ of $N$, between the two complexes $\ker(J(T)	o J(T\setminus C))$. This isomorphism commutes with forgetting supports and with restriction to every open $V\subseteq T$, using $C_V=C	imes_T V$ and the canonical restriction identifications for $R
u_*$ and the two support functors. These restriction identifications also intertwine the derived comparison adjunction units under the canonical inverse-image restriction comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For $C=T$, $b_{T,N}$ is the final-object comparison $R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},R
u_{T,*}N)\cong R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{proet}},N)$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: the comparison functor preserves derived support sections via the direct-image/K-injective kernel identity.

proof.text: Use the existing additive kernel-of-restriction functors and the literal direct-image identities on fixed-coefficient sheaves. The public source imports provide Grothendieck-abelian K-injective resolutions and unbounded right derived functors directly; no transport through ringed-site module categories is needed. Exact comparison inverse image makes its right adjoint preserve K-injectives. Apply the existing canonical rightDerivedFunctorCompIso' to nu_* followed by supported sections, and likewise to final-object evaluation, obtaining b and g.

proof.text: The composite right-derived-functor unit satisfies its defining factorization through the composition isomorphism. Pass from the homotopy-category unit to the complex-level supportResolutionUnit using quotientCompQhIso naturality. This proves the kernel and final-object normalization equations, in fact for every complex. Naturality follows from the canonical derived constructions, with no choice of new representatives.

proof.text: The two underived kernel inclusions commute with the literal direct-image identities. Right-derived natural-transformation functoriality and uniqueness of factorization through the composite derived unit therefore give the forgetting-supports square.

source.place: Paragraph 4; expanded using the canonical source derived-functor and open-adjunction APIs.

proof.text: Open restriction on each site has an exact extension-by-zero left adjoint, by the existing etale and finite-coefficient pro-etale source constructions. Thus restriction preserves K-injectives by adjunction, and is itself exact since it also has a right adjoint. Identify it with inverse image using the existing source restriction isomorphisms. Combining the two canonical composition isomorphisms with the literal direct-image restriction identity and the exact-functor derived comparison constructs rho and proves its resolution-unit equation. This replaces the generic ringed-site localization argument.

source.place: Paragraph 4; expanded using the canonical source derived-functor and open-adjunction APIs.

proof.text: Construct the two ordinary open-support maps by the kernel universal property: restrict a supported section from T to V. The complement of the pulled-back support maps to the complement of the original support, as follows from the range of the second pullback projection. Functoriality of sections and the kernel equation show that the restriction factors through the new kernel. Kernel.lift_ι gives the section equations, naturality follows after cancelling the kernel inclusion, and the etale/pro-etale square is the same kernel map on both sides.

source.place: Paragraph 4; expanded using the canonical source derived-functor and open-adjunction APIs.

proof.text: Derive the ordinary open-support maps using rightDerivedFunctorNatTrans, the composition isomorphism, and the exact-restriction comparison. Their resolution-unit equations follow from the corresponding three defining factorization equations. To prove the open square, test it on K-injective representatives, which suffice by the K-injective description of derived categories. Cancel the invertible resolution-unit maps, use the b, rho, and open-map normalization equations, and apply resolution-unit naturality. Both composites reduce to the complex-level image of the ordinary square from the previous step.

source.place: Paragraph 4; expanded using the canonical source derived-functor and open-adjunction APIs.

proof.text: The specified underived open-pullback comparison satisfies comparisonPullbackOpenUnit. The canonical derived adjunction is the existing mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction, built from Adjunction.derived. Its derivedη_fac_app equation expresses its unit on a complex as the underived unit followed by the right-derived resolution unit and the inverse exact-functor factorization. Test the desired natural-transformation equality on K-injective representatives, apply the rho normalization, exact-functor composition factorization, and the underived unit equation, then cancel the exact-comparison factors. This gives the requested unit square for all unbounded derived objects.

proof.text: At full support, the complement of the identity immersion is empty. The existing empty-cover sheaf condition makes sections over this complement terminal and hence zero in ModuleCat. Consequently both kernel inclusions are isomorphisms by kernel.ι_of_zero. Their derived transformations are isomorphisms, and the forgetting-supports square already proved identifies b with the final-object comparison g.
